non_policy_categories.meaning: The request is malformed or names something that does not exist; refusing it says nothing about whether the intended action was permitted.
A concurrent actor won a race or the target already changed state; the refusal is coordination, not judgement.
The system could not evaluate or persist the request; no policy was applied, so the refusal cannot count as one.
The staged or pushed content failed a declared check (a suite, a linter, a scan); the refusal judges the content, not whether the actor may act, and passing it grants nothing.

completeness.limit: SQLite aborts, host-hook denials and refusing exits of the Weave git hooks are detected mechanically and every one must be claimed here. Every declared command gate must emit its verdict through wv_policy_verdict at its declared site, and every emit must name a declared rule, a decision that rule declares, and a declared site. A command gate that emits nothing is still indistinguishable in code from input validation, so the set of command gates is complete only as far as a manual classification reached: instrumenting v1.0.0 found three gates it had missed. Git-hook refusals inside '# BEGIN source-only' blocks (the evidence lab's E6 gates) are outside this contract as they are outside the release, which cuts them.

excluded_scopes.reason: A host hook that denies before wv is invoked leaves no wv call: there is no call_id, and any identity joining it to one would be minted by the hook itself, which is the self-declared evidence the attempt journal exists to remove. Such denials are outside the denominator by declaration, and are never written as wv call rows.

A Weave git hook decides whether a commit or push proceeds outside any wv call. The wv subprocesses it runs are not proof of the commit's outcome: git can still fail, or the hook be skipped, after they return, and nothing joins them to a commit identity. Git events stay outside the denominator until an independently grounded event identity exists, and their rules are reported as outside evidence rather than exercised or gapped.

denominator.rationale: The E1 denominator is wv calls: a call counts only when the attempt journal holds its call_started event, written by wv before dispatch. wv calls a hook launches (source=hook, such as prune or load) are wv calls and stay in. What the exclusion costs: E1 does not measure the host-hook counterweight layer until hooks can carry an identity they did not create; until then that layer's effect is unmeasured, not zero.

rules.summary: A non-epic node may not be created without a parent while an epic is open, because it would be orphaned.
A node created directly as active must already carry done criteria and a risk assessment.
Reconstructing a node by explicit id may not overwrite a node that still exists.
Initialising may not replace a database that already holds nodes.
A close may not proceed without quality scan data for the quality gates to judge; missing evidence fails closed.
A finding node may not close without a catalogued violation_type.

sites.anchor: finding node requires violation_type before close

rules.summary: A close may scope its completion only to files attributed to the node, under a fresh attempt identity.
rules.notes: The SQLite clause is split in the close receipt: a completion_scope with no usable shape (not an array, empty, a non-text or empty entry) is recorded as input_validation, while a stale attempt identity or a file the node never touched is a deny with clause.reason naming which. The trigger keeps one abort message because it is only the backstop.

rules.summary: A close must record a learning unless it is declared trivial.
A node marked as waiting for human verification may not close until that is acknowledged.
rules.notes: The acknowledging flag is named for learning overlap, not for pending verification; recorded as observed rather than as intended.

rules.summary: A node reserved for a counted evidence capture may not be claimed as ordinary work.
A done node may be reopened only by an explicit reopen, never implicitly by a claim or an update.
Taking over a node another agent has claimed requires an explicit override, which is recorded; a claim under an unverifiable session identity is refused.
rules.notes: The takeover (--force) and the continuation of this actor's own pre-session coarse claim (--continue) are policy events, each appended to metadata.claim_history; --continue on anyone else's claim is denied, and so is any claim when a harness that carries a session id did not supply it (wv-99978b). A claim refused because another agent holds the node is recorded as expected_conflict: the atomic claim cannot tell a live holder from a race this call just lost.

rules.summary: A node with child nodes may not be deleted without explicit intent, because it would orphan them.
Blocking edges may not form a self-loop or a cycle.

An edge may not break its type's invariant (contracts/edge-types-v1.json): no self-edge, acyclic blocks and implements, supersedes old to new unless declared, resolves to a finding, addresses from the newer node.
A node may not close over an open implements child that is not parked, linked by resolves, or under another open parent.
A sync may not overwrite the committed graph with a dump far smaller than it, the signature of a wiped or partial hot zone.
rules.notes: The floor guard also runs when another operation auto-syncs. There the sync is a side effect, not the call's operation: a refusal surfaces as that sync step's failure and is not recorded as a counted decision of the enclosing call (wv-15422b). Only an explicit wv sync records this rule's verdict.

rules.summary: Deltas may not be compacted while agents hold claims that may not have replayed them.
A causal cutover may not run while agents hold claims.
Recovery may not complete a close that was never durably recorded.
Scaffolding and repair may write only into a repository classified as owned, never into vendored upstream code.

bypass.how: classify the repository as owned with wv repo-class set owned

rules.summary: Classifying a remote-bearing repository as owned against autodetection requires acknowledging it is an intentional fork.
A node whose text matches an open node, or one closed in the last 30 days, is refused as a likely duplicate.
rules.notes: Not applied to an add with --parent: decomposition shares vocabulary with its parent by design. quick has no bypass.

rules.summary: Initialising through a symlinked Weave directory is refused, because it writes graph state outside the repository.
A learning that overlaps or contradicts an existing one is recorded as an advisory; it never blocks the close.
A close may not complete while a file it touched exceeds the McCabe complexity threshold.

rules.summary: A commit proceeds only under an active node claimed by the actor committing it.

bypass.how: nothing is staged, or only graph state as the hook's classifier decides it (state.sql, nodes/edges jsonl, deltas, trails); never all of .weave/, and with the classifier missing, nothing counts as graph state
no executable wv is found and neither HEAD nor the index tracks .weave/ (not Weave-managed)

rules.notes: Identity source: wv list --status=active --claimed-by=current, which resolves the actor as resolve_agent_id does for the Weave-ID trailers: WV_AGENT_ID if set, otherwise <harness>-<host>-<user>-s<sid12> when the harness carries a session id (Claude Code, Codex; WV_SESSION_IDENTITY=0 turns this off), else <harness>-<host>-<user> from the committing process's environment, with human when no agent harness is detected. A harness session whose id is missing fails the listing (wv-99978b). One identity policy for admission and attribution; they remain separate hooks and queries. Failure behaviour: a listing that fails reads as no claim, so admission fails closed. Continuing another actor's node is wv work <id> --force, which claim_ownership records as a takeover; it is not a bypass. Admission is session-owned where the harness carries a session id, and actor-owned for a human shell, Copilot or WV_SESSION_IDENTITY=0 (wv-99978b, design wv-d7f53e). A pre-session coarse claim is resumed with wv work <id> --continue. With no node active at all the second site refuses (the discover-phase message). Removed as exemptions (wv-68aeff): WV_AUTO_CHECKPOINT_ACTIVE and WV_STYLE_COMMIT (a flag is not authority), the whitespace-only shortcut (git diff -w cannot show semantic equivalence), and the closing phase (repository-shared; the graph commit it existed for is graph state). With no wv in a Weave-managed repository a substantive commit is refused. A commit cannot remove its own enforcement prerequisite (wv-49b687): Weave management, the shellcheck scope declaration, .shellcheckrc, the memory-parity map row and the release leak checker count when HEAD or the index has them, so staging their deletion or relaxation does not disable them for that commit.

rules.summary: The heavy tier a push owes runs against exactly the commit being pushed.

bypass.how: no executable wv, no [heavy] section in the test map, or no pushed file selects a heavy suite

sites.anchor: so what is tested is what is pushed.
Commit or stash them, then push again.

rules.notes: A ref that is not HEAD, or tracked files differing from the tip, would have the heavy tier test something other than what is pushed.

non_policy_sites.summary: A hook payload that cannot be parsed is refused before any rule runs.
Pre-close verification that times out denies the close without evaluating it.

A close receipt or exemption bypass that names no declared rule, and the policy trigger refusing a close its receipt allowed, are the receipt and the trigger disagreeing: no single decision was made, so neither counts as one. A claim whose write failed or did not persist (wv-03d775) is likewise a failure, not a decision.
Gate-family commands refuse a missing or unknown node, a malformed --id, and malformed or inapplicable --completion-files.
A claim lost to another agent, a close of a node already closed, and a node that changed state mid-close are conflicts, not decisions.

Delta replay re-applies a close another actor already decided, so it is not a close decision of the load or sync call replaying it, and every close that is one (done, ship, batch-done, update, bulk-update, quick, resolve) is judged by the close receipt first. If the local close trigger refuses a replayed close, the replay failed; nothing was decided.

Another Weave gate holds this checkout (wv-c5500d): the pre-commit or pre-push gate refuses to start beside it, naming the holder. One gate at a time per checkout is a conflict over shared git state and scratch, not a judgement of the content.
